messages.subject: Analysing 50+ days of accelerometry
parts:
Hi,

I've gone through some previous posts where people have flagged related issues, and I saw a response back in April about a potential update to allow more than 7 days output from part 5. Our protocol involves continuous GENEActiv wear for 8 weeks.... Even for participants who wore the monitor continuously (as I can see from part 2 output), only ~7days are visible from part 5. 

Is there an update on the horizon to allow analysis of long-term monitoring?

I'm not experienced with R so I've changed as little as possible, but if it helps, the code I'm using is:

library(GGIR)
g.shell.GGIR(#=======================================
             # INPUT NEEDED:
             mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
        datadir="D:/RCT2-test",
        outputdir="D:/RCT2-test",

             f0=1, f1=1,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 1:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
             do.enmo = TRUE,             do.anglez=TRUE,
             chunksize=1,                printsummary=TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2:
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 2,               ndayswindow=7,
             hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
             maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 10,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),
             qwindow=c(0,24),
             ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),
             mvpathreshold =c(100,120),
             bout.metric = 4,
             closedbout=FALSE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 3:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Sleep detection
             timethreshold= c(5),        anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 4:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Integrating sleep log (if available) with sleep detection
             # storing day and person specific summaries of sleep
             excludefirstlast = TRUE,
             includenightcrit = 16,
             def.noc.sleep = c(),
             #loglocation= " ",
             outliers.only = TRUE,
             criterror = 4,
             relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
             sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
             colid=1,
             coln1=2,
             do.visual = TRUE,
             nnights = 9,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5:
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             #-------------------------------
             threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),
             boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1),   timewindow = c("WW"),
             #-----------------------------------
             # Report generation
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Generating reports based on meta-data
             do.report=c(2,4,5),
             visualreport=TRUE,     dofirstpage = TRUE,
             viewingwindow=1)

Kind regards,

Justin

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: Analysing 50+ days of accelerometry
parts:
Hi Justin,

I'm not sure if GGIR can handle this number of days, but I cannot see the reason why it cannot do it. Let's try to change some parameters in your function call, and the let us now if this worked.

Change the next parameters as follows:

  • Remove the argument 'ndayswindow' from part2, it would only be useful if 'strategy' is set to 3.
  • Remove the argument 'maxdur' from part2, it would only be useful if 'strategy' is set to 1.
  • I would set 'includedaycrit' to 16, since you have 'includenightcrit = 16' in part4
  • Remove the arguments 'nnights', 'sleeplogidnum', 'colid' and 'coln1' from part4 (they are related to the use of a sleeplog and I think you are not using sleeplog, right?
Can you also tell if g.part4 is giving you estimates for all of the nights? Or only for 7 days?

Best,
Jairo

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: Analysing 50+ days of accelerometry
parts:
The problem here was that the default value for the argument 'nnights' is 7, so the analysis is constrained to 7 days by default. Setting the argument 'nnights = c()' in g.part4 solved this and all the nights were included in the analyses.

I'm posting this here in case anyone finds this helpful.

Best,
Jairo

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Analysing 50+ days of accelerometry
parts:
Hi Justin,

There is no day limit to part 4 or 5, only in part 2 there is an arbitrary limit of 26 weeks.
The nnpp = 40 which Vahan found in the code does not apply here. It relates to argument do.visual in function g.part4. This creates a pdf with 40 nights per page from an entire study. If there are more nights it will simply keep creating new pages in the pdf until all nights are visualised.

Do you get 38 days for both the MM and WW reports in part5?
I think that changing excludefirstlast = TRUE to excludefirstlast = FALSE will give you the 40 days of data.

Note that with excludefirstlast = TRUE you tell GGIR to ignore the first and last night, which then influences the number of days/nights part5 can work with. As a result, it is not surprising to have 2 nights/days less in part 5 compared with part 2 for example.

Best, Vincent
